!3 CSV: the three row shapes
The first line is the header. Columns are compared by name, so their order does not matter. The separator is set with '''separator''' (here a semicolon; '''tab''' stands for a tab; a .tsv file defaults to tab). The e2e files have their rows in another order, so the file-to-file row uses '''key'''.

|script|csv comparison|
|separator|;|
|key|id|
|check|compare file|src/test/resources/e2e/expected/export.csv|to file|src/test/resources/e2e/actual/export.csv|OK|
|ordered|
|note|file to inline content, in {{{ }}}: one label holds the separator and a line break inside quotes|
|check|compare file|src/test/resources/e2e/expected/export.csv|to|{{{
label;amount;id
Widget;10.00;1
"Gadget; large
blue";99;2
Gizmo;5.5;3
}}}|OK|
|note|inline to inline|
|check|compare;|{{{id;v
1;a}}}|{{{v;id
a;1}}}|OK|
|check not|compare;|{{{id;v
1;a}}}|{{{id;v
1;b}}}|OK|
|separator|tab|
|check|compare;|{{{id	v
1	a}}}|{{{v	id
a	1}}}|OK|
